cards.front: Complete the rule: An approved Illinois driver-education course includes at least.
cards.back: An approved Illinois driver-education course includes at least thirty classroom hours and six hours driving a regular passenger vehicle with an instructor.
cards.memory_hook: Classroom plus behind the wheel minimums

cards.front: Complete the rule: An applicant aged fifteen through seventeen needs provider.
cards.back: An applicant aged fifteen through seventeen needs provider evidence of enrollment in approved driver education or a course starting within thirty days to receive an instruction permit.
cards.memory_hook: Young permit links to approved education

cards.front: Complete the rule: For ages fifteen through seventeen, an instruction permit.
cards.back: For ages fifteen through seventeen, an instruction permit lasts twenty-four months and must be held for nine consecutive months before licensing.
cards.memory_hook: Permit life differs from holding period

cards.front: Complete the rule: Beginning at seventeen years and three months, an.
cards.back: Beginning at seventeen years and three months, an applicant may seek an instruction permit without taking driver education.
cards.memory_hook: Later teen permit has education exception

cards.front: Complete the rule: A permit applicant must pass the vision and.
cards.back: A permit applicant must pass the vision and written examinations for the requested license class, and those results remain valid until the permit expires.
cards.memory_hook: Permit exams match requested class

cards.front: Complete the rule: An instruction permit allows behind-the-wheel.
cards.back: An instruction permit allows behind-the-wheel instruction in the driver-education course.
cards.memory_hook: Permit supports instructor led practice

cards.front: Complete the rule: Other permit practice requires a parent, guardian or.
cards.back: Other permit practice requires a parent, guardian or responsible adult who is at least twenty-one, holds a valid license and has a year of driving experience, seated beside the learner in front.
cards.memory_hook: Qualified supervisor sits beside learner

cards.front: Complete the rule: After finishing driver education, a permit holder may.
cards.back: After finishing driver education, a permit holder may continue practicing under the same direct adult supervision.
cards.memory_hook: Course completion does not end supervision

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before licensing at sixteen, an applicant younger than.
cards.back: Before licensing at sixteen, an applicant younger than eighteen must complete fifty supervised practice hours, including ten at night, in addition to driver-education training.
cards.memory_hook: Fifty practice hours include ten nighttime

cards.front: Complete the rule: Licenses for people younger than twenty-one.
cards.back: Licenses for people younger than twenty-one use a vertical layout with distinguishing features.
cards.memory_hook: Young driver license is vertical

cards.front: Complete the rule: An applicant younger than eighteen brings the instruction.
cards.back: An applicant younger than eighteen brings the instruction permit, acceptable identity documents, a properly signed fifty-hour log and any applicable minor-consent affidavit or Cooperative Driver Testing Certificate.
cards.memory_hook: Young applicant brings records and consent

cards.front: Complete the rule: A young applicant requesting REAL ID must also.
cards.back: A young applicant requesting REAL ID must also provide the full first-time REAL ID identity-document set.
cards.memory_hook: Youth pathway keeps REAL ID documents

cards.front: Complete the rule: License issuance requires the agency to receive the.
cards.back: License issuance requires the agency to receive the driver-education completion notice and post it to the applicant’s driving record.
cards.memory_hook: Completion must reach driving record

cards.front: Complete the rule: A student selected by a birthday-based spot-check date.
cards.back: A student selected by a birthday-based spot-check date must pass a facility road test even after passing the instructor’s road test.
cards.memory_hook: Spot check can require another road

cards.front: Complete the rule: An applicant licensed before the instruction permit.
cards.back: An applicant licensed before the instruction permit expires does not pay an additional license-application fee.
cards.memory_hook: Unexpired permit avoids additional fee

cards.front: Complete the rule: A high-school student completing accredited classroom and driving.
cards.back: A high-school student completing accredited classroom and driving instruction with a combined A or B grade may qualify for exemption from the agency’s road test through cooperative testing.
cards.memory_hook: Qualifying school performance may waive agency

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Cooperative Driver Testing Certificate follows a successful.
cards.back: A Cooperative Driver Testing Certificate follows a successful driving examination and needs both the instructor’s signature and the parent’s or guardian’s signature.
cards.memory_hook: Cooperative certificate needs both signatures

cards.front: Complete the rule: The cooperative-testing certificate expires with the instruction permit.
cards.back: The cooperative-testing certificate expires with the instruction permit, cannot be extended and must be presented when applying for the license.
cards.memory_hook: Certificate shares permit expiry

cards.front: Complete the rule: A dropout younger than eighteen needs a qualifying.
cards.back: A dropout younger than eighteen needs a qualifying exception before the education-completion notation can be added: verified alternative-program enrollment, a GED, eight passed courses in the preceding two semesters or the required written consents.
cards.memory_hook: Dropout notation requires listed exception

cards.front: Complete the rule: The dropout-consent exception requires written consent from.
cards.back: The dropout-consent exception requires written consent from the parent or guardian and the regional superintendent.
cards.memory_hook: Dropout consent has two sources

cards.front: Complete the rule: A local superintendent or chief school administrator may.
cards.back: A local superintendent or chief school administrator may waive dropout conditions considered contrary to the student’s best interest.
cards.memory_hook: School administrator may waive conditions

cards.front: Complete the rule: A first-time applicant aged eighteen through twenty who.
cards.back: A first-time applicant aged eighteen through twenty who has neither a previous license nor approved driver education must complete a six-hour adult driver-education course.
cards.memory_hook: Young adult without prior qualification six

cards.front: Complete the rule: The adult course must come from an agency-certified.
cards.back: The adult course must come from an agency-certified provider; classroom or online delivery depends on that provider’s certification, and an uncertified course is not accepted.
cards.memory_hook: Provider certification controls course acceptance

cards.front: Complete the rule: Illinois graduated licensing covers ages fifteen through twenty.
cards.back: Illinois graduated licensing covers ages fifteen through twenty through three progressive phases, with advancement dependent on driving behavior.
cards.memory_hook: Progression depends on conduct

decks.module: Permit restrictions and Initial license restrictions

cards.front: Complete the rule: During the permit phase, nighttime restrictions run from.
cards.back: During the permit phase, nighttime restrictions run from ten at night until six in the morning Sunday through Thursday and from eleven at night until six Friday and Saturday, subject to differing local curfews.
cards.memory_hook: Permit nighttime limits vary by weekday

cards.front: Complete the rule: The permit phase requires at least nine months.
cards.back: The permit phase requires at least nine months and fifty supervised practice hours, including ten after dark, with a licensed parent or adult at least twenty-one.
cards.memory_hook: Permit phase combines time and practice

cards.front: Complete the rule: The nine-month permit phase must be free of.
cards.back: The nine-month permit phase must be free of driving infractions, underage alcohol convictions and court supervision.
cards.memory_hook: Permit phase requires clean conduct

cards.front: Complete the rule: Permit-phase passengers are limited to one in the.
cards.back: Permit-phase passengers are limited to one in the front and the number of available safety belts in the rear.
cards.memory_hook: Passenger limit follows seating and belts

cards.front: Complete the rule: A driver younger than nineteen cannot use a.
cards.back: A driver younger than nineteen cannot use a cellphone or wireless device while driving, including hands-free use, except an emergency contact with police, a health-care provider or an emergency-services agency.
cards.memory_hook: Under nineteen emergency contact exception only

cards.front: Complete the rule: For initial license holders aged sixteen or seventeen.
cards.back: For initial license holders aged sixteen or seventeen, nighttime restrictions use ten-to-six Sunday through Thursday and eleven-to-six Friday and Saturday, with local curfews potentially different.
cards.memory_hook: Initial license keeps nighttime restrictions

cards.front: Complete the rule: An initial license holder must keep six conviction-free.
cards.back: An initial license holder must keep six conviction-free months before turning eighteen; a conviction in this phase can extend restrictions beyond the eighteenth birthday.
cards.memory_hook: Conviction can extend initial restrictions

cards.front: Complete the rule: Until the earlier of twelve licensed months or.
cards.back: Until the earlier of twelve licensed months or age eighteen, only one passenger younger than twenty is allowed unless the passengers are the driver’s siblings, stepsiblings, children or stepchildren.
cards.memory_hook: First year young passenger rule has

decks.module: Initial license restrictions and Young-driver sanctions

cards.front: Complete the rule: After the initial young-passenger period, passengers remain limited.
cards.back: After the initial young-passenger period, passengers remain limited to one front-seat occupant and the number of rear safety belts.
cards.memory_hook: Later passenger limit follows seats and

cards.front: Complete the rule: Full licensing at ages eighteen through twenty removes.
cards.back: Full licensing at ages eighteen through twenty removes age-based restrictions unless the driver failed to advance out of the initial phase; the under-nineteen wireless restriction still applies.
cards.memory_hook: Full phase retains stated exceptions

cards.front: Complete the rule: Licensing at sixteen or seventeen requires written parental.
cards.back: Licensing at sixteen or seventeen requires written parental or guardian consent, and the person who gave it may cancel the license for any reason before the driver turns eighteen.
cards.memory_hook: Consent giver can cancel minor license

cards.front: Complete the rule: After consent is withdrawn, privileges cannot return until.
cards.back: After consent is withdrawn, privileges cannot return until that person consents again or the driver turns eighteen, whichever comes first; the driver must reapply, take required exams and pay applicable fees.
cards.memory_hook: Restored consent still requires reapplication

cards.front: Complete the rule: A parent or guardian can view an under-eighteen.
cards.back: A parent or guardian can view an under-eighteen permit or graduated-license holder’s driving record free online using the agency-provided personal identification number.
cards.memory_hook: Parent has free minor record access

cards.front: Complete the rule: A valid permit holder younger than twenty-one and.
cards.back: A valid permit holder younger than twenty-one and the parent or guardian can use the permit number online to check whether high-school driver-education completion is recorded.
cards.memory_hook: Permit number checks education posting

cards.front: Complete the rule: The agency offers a Parent-Teen Driving Guide and.
cards.back: The agency offers a Parent-Teen Driving Guide and a voluntary driving contract to help families set learning expectations and boundaries.
cards.memory_hook: Guide and voluntary contract support practice

cards.front: Complete the rule: A driver younger than twenty-one is limited to.
cards.back: A driver younger than twenty-one is limited to one court supervision for serious traffic offenses and must attend traffic safety school to obtain supervision for a traffic violation.
cards.memory_hook: Supervision is limited and requires school

cards.front: Complete the rule: A driver younger than eighteen seeking court supervision.
cards.back: A driver younger than eighteen seeking court supervision for a traffic violation must appear with a parent or guardian.
cards.memory_hook: Minor supervision needs parent in court

cards.front: Complete the rule: Court supervision for certain alcohol offenses can postpone.
cards.back: Court supervision for certain alcohol offenses can postpone a minor’s full graduated license for nine months.
cards.memory_hook: Alcohol supervision delays full license

cards.front: Complete the rule: For a driver younger than twenty-one, at least.
cards.back: For a driver younger than twenty-one, at least two moving-violation convictions within twenty-four months lead to a license suspension of at least thirty days, with duration depending on offense seriousness.
cards.memory_hook: Repeated young driver violations suspend license

cards.front: Complete the rule: Reinstatement after a young-driver suspension may require remedial.
cards.back: Reinstatement after a young-driver suspension may require remedial driver education, and eligibility for a restricted permit during suspension is not guaranteed.
cards.memory_hook: Remedial course possible permit not assured

cards.front: Complete the rule: An under-twenty-one vehicle occupant receiving court supervision for.
cards.back: An under-twenty-one vehicle occupant receiving court supervision for possessing, consuming, buying or receiving alcohol faces a three-month license suspension; conviction brings at least six months.
cards.memory_hook: Alcohol sanction distinguishes supervision and conviction

cards.front: Complete the rule: A permit or initial-phase driver younger than eighteen.
cards.back: A permit or initial-phase driver younger than eighteen may have driving privileges suspended for violating the nighttime driving restriction.
cards.memory_hook: Night restriction violation can suspend privileges

cards.front: Complete the rule: An under-eighteen driver charged after a crash causing.
cards.back: An under-eighteen driver charged after a crash causing serious injury or death may be denied license issuance or renewal even if alcohol was not involved.
cards.memory_hook: Serious crash can block minor licensing

cards.front: Complete the rule: An unresolved court traffic citation can prevent.
cards.back: An unresolved court traffic citation can prevent license issuance for someone younger than eighteen.
cards.memory_hook: Pending citation can block issuance
